{"code": "print("\nChecking for sentinel values in customer_age...")
print(df[df['customer_age'] == -1]['customer_age'].count(), "rows with age = -1")

print("\nChecking for QA orders in revenue...")
# QA orders have revenue = 999999.99
qa_orders = df[df['revenue'] == '999999.99']
print(f"{len(qa_orders)} QA orders found.")

print("\nChecking for refunded orders...")
refunded = df[df['status'] == 'refunded']
print(f"{len(refunded)} refunded orders found.")

# Note: We are only interested in loyal customers, and for conversion, we only care about 'converted' == 1
# But we must exclude QA and refunded orders for accurate conversion rate

# Filter for loyal customers
loyal_df = df[df['customer_segment'] == 'loyal']

# Exclude QA orders and refunded orders
valid_loyal = loyal_df[~((loyal_df['revenue'] == '999999.99') | (loyal_df['status'] == 'refunded'))]

print(f"\nAfter filtering: {len(valid_loyal)} valid loyal orders remain out of {len(loyal_df)}.")

# Now calculate conversion rate: fraction of valid loyal orders where converted == 1
converted_count = valid_loyal['converted'].sum()
total_count = len(valid_loyal)
conversion_rate = converted_count / total_count

print(f"Converted: {converted_count} out of {total_count} → {conversion_rate:.4f}")"}
